issues.description: The marked answer (index 2, option C) uses `helm rollback my-release` with no REVISION argument. In Helm 3.x, `helm rollback` requires a RELEASE name and takes an optional REVISION positional argument. However, the behavior when REVISION is omitted varies across Helm 3 minor versions: some versions return an error ('requires 2 arguments'), while newer versions (3.12+) accept it and default to the previous revision. Per the review guidelines, `helm rollback RELEASE 0` is the canonical way to roll back to the previous release without specifying a numbered revision. Option C's command may fail on common Helm 3 versions in production. Meanwhile, option B (`helm rollback my-release 1`) is valid syntax and would be correct if this was the first upgrade (rolling back to the original install, which IS the previous revision). Since the question says 'After running helm upgrade', this implies there was exactly one upgrade from the initial install, making revision 1 the previous revision. Both options B and C would achieve the same result in this scenario, but option C uses potentially unreliable syntax while option B uses guaranteed-valid syntax with a correct description.
issues.suggested_fix: Change option C to use `helm rollback my-release 0` which is explicitly valid per Helm docs and the review guidelines (revision 0 = previous release). Update the explanation to note that revision 0 is a special value meaning 'roll back to the immediately previous release'. This eliminates any ambiguity about whether omitting the revision argument is valid, while clearly distinguishing option C (roll back to previous, wherever that is) from option B (roll back to revision 1 specifically).
